text: Hemeralopia [Gr. hmera , day, + wy , eye]: Ger. Hemeralopie , Nachtblindheit ; Fr. héméralopie ; Ital. emeralopia . This term and the term nyctalopia are used by different authors in exactly opposite senses, according as the term is regarded as etymologically equivalent to 'seeing at daytime,' or 'blind at daytime'; 'seeing at night-time,' or 'blind at night-time.' Nyctalopia is used by ancient and mediaeval writers as the equivalent of night-blindness. The conditions referred to are described under the terms DAY-BLINDNESS and NIGHT-BLINDNESS (q.v.). See also Hemeralopia and Nyctalopia in Quain's Dictionary of Medicine . ( J.J. )
